site.title: RegRisk Radar
site.tagline: Daily facts-only regulatory radar — crypto, gaming, payments & fintech. Verified against primary sources.
site.disclaimer: RegRisk Radar is regulatory-risk intelligence provided for general informational purposes only. It is not legal advice and does not create an attorney-client relationship; it is not investment, tax, or financial advice. Regulatory matters are fact-specific and change quickly — consult qualified counsel about your situation. Primary sources are linked; verify before acting.

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate (17 Democrats)
items.title: Senate Democrats ask Appropriations Committee to bar CFTC from funding state prediction market preemption suits
items.facts: On June 26, 2026, seventeen Democratic senators — led by Senators Blumenthal (D-CT), Merkley (D-OR), Schiff (D-CA), and Padilla (D-CA), joined by Senators Cantwell, Cortez Masto, Durbin, Heinrich, Hickenlooper, Hirono, Luján, Murphy, Rosen, Schatz, Smith, Warren, and Whitehouse — sent a letter to the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government requesting that the Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations bill prohibit the Commodity Futures Trading Commission from using federal funds to prevent states and Tribes from enforcing their gambling laws and gaming compacts against online prediction markets. The letter identifies eight states already sued by the CFTC (Connecticut, Illinois, Arizona, Wisconsin, New York, Minnesota, Rhode Island, and New Mexico) and states: 'Through engaging in this campaign of litigation and intimidation, the CFTC risks becoming an instrument and enabler of online prediction markets' efforts to bypass states' consumer protections and oversight, creating a race-to-the-bottom in gambling.'
items.source_label: Sen. Schiff Press Release — schiff.senate.gov (June 26, 2026; primary source retrieved)
items.relevant_to: Prediction market operators; gaming, fintech, and crypto platforms with US state regulatory exposure

items.issuing_body: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), in coordination with FinCEN and OFAC
items.title: OCC proposes AML/CFT and sanctions compliance program rules for permitted payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act (Federal Register 2026-12692)
items.facts: On June 24, 2026, the OCC — in coordination with Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) — published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking in the Federal Register (document 2026-12692) proposing Bank Secrecy Act and sanctions compliance program standards for permitted payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs) under the GENIUS Act. The proposal builds on a March 2, 2026 proposed rule; a public comment period is open.
items.source_label: Federal Register — OCC NPRM document 2026-12692 (published June 24, 2026; primary source retrieved)
items.relevant_to: permitted payment stablecoin issuers, crypto exchanges and custodians, BSA/AML compliance teams

items.issuing_body: State of Iowa (Governor Kim Reynolds)
items.title: Iowa SF 2289 grants Iowa Racing and Gaming Commission cease-and-desist and injunctive relief powers over unlicensed sweepstakes casinos; effective July 1, 2026
items.facts: Iowa Governor Kim Reynolds signed Senate File 2289 on May 15, 2026. Effective July 1, 2026, the law grants the Iowa Racing and Gaming Commission authority to issue cease-and-desist orders and seek injunctive relief against unlicensed online sweepstakes casino operators. Platforms including High 5 Casino, Baba Casino, and Lucky Bunny Casino have announced they will cut off Iowa player access effective June 30–July 1, 2026.
items.source_label: Iowa Legislature — SF 2289 bill page (legis.iowa.gov; primary source retrieved)
items.relevant_to: sweepstakes casino operators, dual-currency gaming platforms serving Iowa players, gaming compliance teams

items.issuing_body: CFTC
items.title: CFTC proposes formal data-reporting rules for event contracts, ending eight-plus years of no-action relief (NPRM 9261-26)
items.facts: On June 25, 2026, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (Press Release 9261-26) proposing amendments to Parts 15, 16, and 17 of CFTC regulations to establish an alternate data-reporting framework for fully collateralized event contracts. The proposal would require reporting markets, futures commission merchants (FCMs), clearing members, and foreign brokers to report event contracts under Parts 15–18 of the CFTC's regulations rather than under Parts 38, 39, 43, and 45, replacing an informal reporting regime that has operated under staff no-action letters since 2017. A public comment period is open; the comment deadline will be set in the Federal Register notice.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9261-26 (June 25, 2026)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, FCMs, clearing members, foreign brokers dealing in event contracts

items.issuing_body: KalshiEx LLC (plaintiff) v. Governor JB Pritzker, Attorney General Kwame Raoul, Illinois Gaming Board — U.S. District Court, Northern District of Illinois
items.title: Kalshi files federal lawsuit against Illinois over SB3019's 15% sports prediction market gross receipts tax and state licensing requirement for DCMs; TRO and PI sought ahead of July 1 effective date
items.facts: Kalshi filed a 31-page federal complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois on June 23, 2026, naming Governor JB Pritzker, Attorney General Kwame Raoul, and five Illinois Gaming Board officials as defendants. SB3019 imposes: (a) a 15% gross-receipts tax on sports prediction market revenues; (b) a state licensing requirement for CFTC-registered designated contract markets (DCMs). Both provisions take effect July 1, 2026. Kalshi argues both provisions are preempted by the Commodity Exchange Act's exclusive-jurisdiction clause (7 U.S.C. § 2(a)(1)(A)). The complaint seeks a temporary restraining order, preliminary injunction, and permanent injunction.
items.source_label: Courthouse News Service (June 24, 2026; corroborated by The Block, SBC Americas, CryptoTimes, Crain's Chicago Business)
items.relevant_to: CFTC-registered DCMs, prediction-market operators, payment processors supporting prediction markets, crypto exchanges with Illinois nexus

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate (Senator Cynthia Lummis / CLARITY Act floor scheduling)
items.title: Lummis publicly commits to CLARITY Act Senate floor vote in July; week of July 13 targeted; law enforcement coalition and Catholic leaders file Section 604 opposition letters
items.facts: Senator Cynthia Lummis stated on Fox Business's 'Mornings with Maria' on June 24, 2026 that the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act will reach the Senate floor in July, with the week of July 13 identified as the target window. Galaxy Research put passage-before-recess probability at approximately 60%. The House Financial Services Committee has scheduled a July 17, 2026 field hearing titled 'Building the Future of Finance: How the CLARITY Act Unlocks Innovation.' On June 23, 2026, a law enforcement coalition wrote to Acting AG Todd Blanche opposing Section 604. The bill still requires approximately seven Democratic votes to clear the 60-vote cloture threshold.
items.source_label: The Defiant/Converge (June 24, 2026; corroborated by The Block and PYMNTS)
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, stablecoin issuers, prediction-market platforms, DeFi protocols, digital asset market participants

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate (Senate Banking Committee markup; Senate Legislative Calendar No. 423) / House Agriculture digital-assets subcommittee (Rep. Dusty Johnson statement)
items.title: CLARITY Act placed on Senate Legislative Calendar No. 423; House Agriculture chair commits to fast follow; August recess is the operative deadline; seven Democratic votes remain the gap to cloture
items.facts: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act has been placed on the U.S. Senate Legislative Calendar as Calendar No. 423, following a 15-9 Senate Banking Committee markup on May 14, 2026. House Agriculture digital-assets subcommittee chair Rep. Dusty Johnson stated the House will move immediately on a companion measure if the Senate passes the bill before the August recess. The bill requires approximately 60 votes to clear a Senate filibuster — about seven Democratic votes beyond full Republican unity.
items.source_label: The Defiant (June 19, 2026; corroborated by PYMNTS.com, Yahoo Finance, CoinPedia, and Seeking Alpha)
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, digital-asset market participants, stablecoin issuers, prediction-market platforms, brokerages, DeFi protocols, fintech companies

items.issuing_body: American Gaming Association, Indian Gaming Association, AFL-CIO Hotel and Gaming Trades Council, UNITE HERE (coalition letter to U.S. Senate, June 16, 2026)
items.title: AGA, tribal gaming groups, and labor unions send Senate letter demanding CLARITY Act include explicit ban on prediction-market sports event contracts
items.facts: On June 16, 2026, a coalition led by the AGA, the Indian Gaming Association, the AFL-CIO's Hotel and Gaming Trades Council, and UNITE HERE sent a letter to the U.S. Senate urging legislators to amend the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act to include explicit language barring prediction markets from offering sports and casino-style event contracts. The AGA has separately estimated states have lost roughly $1 billion in gaming tax revenue to prediction markets since the start of 2025.
items.source_label: The Defiant (June 17, 2026; corroborated by CryptoNews, AMBCrypto, Sportsbook Review, Yogonet, BanklessTimes, and Covers.com)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market operators, gaming operators, tribal gaming entities, sportsbooks, CFTC-registered entities

items.issuing_body: Kentucky Office of the Attorney General (Russell Coleman) — Franklin Circuit Court
items.title: Kentucky AG sues Kalshi, Polymarket, and VGW alleging illegal unlicensed gambling operations
items.facts: On June 17, 2026, Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman filed lawsuits in Franklin Circuit Court against prediction-market operators Kalshi and Polymarket and against online sweepstakes-casino operator VGW (operator of Chumba Casino, Global Poker, and LuckyLand Slots), alleging the companies are conducting illegal, unlicensed gambling operations within the Commonwealth. The suits seek temporary and permanent injunctive relief and all recoverable damages available to the Commonwealth.
items.source_label: Covers (June 19, 2026; corroborated by Gambling Insider, Gambling News, LEX18, Yogonet, PlayUSA, LINK nky)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market operators, sweepstakes / social-casino operators, sportsbooks, crypto exchanges, payment processors serving these platforms

items.issuing_body: CFTC — U.S. District Court, Northern District of Illinois
items.title: CFTC amends its Illinois lawsuit and seeks a preliminary injunction against the state's new 'exchange wager' prediction-market tax
items.facts: The CFTC amended its lawsuit against the State of Illinois (N.D. Illinois, No. 1:26-cv-03659, originally filed April 2, 2026) after Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker signed a budget creating a new tax structure for prediction markets. The amended complaint challenges Illinois's new 'exchange wager' provisions; the new Illinois law would impose transaction fees ranging from 1.75% to 3.5% on sports event contracts. The CFTC also filed a motion for a preliminary injunction.
items.source_label: Gambling Insider (June 19, 2026 weekly roundup)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market / event-contract platforms, crypto derivatives exchanges, CFTC registrants, tax and compliance teams

items.issuing_body: Matthew Mazza (plaintiff) — U.S. District Court, Northern District of California
items.title: Proposed class action alleges Robinhood runs an unlicensed sports-gambling operation through its prediction-markets hub
items.facts: On June 10, 2026, a proposed class action (Mazza v. Robinhood) was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California against Robinhood Markets, Inc. and its subsidiary Robinhood Derivatives, alleging the company operates an unlicensed, illegal sports-gambling operation. The named plaintiff alleges he lost approximately $400,000 in fees, commissions, and wagers in 2025-2026.
items.source_label: Casino.org (corroborated by Bloomberg Law, Sportsbook Review, Gambling News, CDC Gaming)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market operators, brokerages offering event contracts, fintech platforms, consumer-protection and compliance teams

items.issuing_body: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
items.title: Sixth Circuit consolidates the Ohio (Kalshi v. Schuler) and Tennessee prediction-market appeals
items.facts: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit consolidated Kalshi's Ohio appeal (KalshiEx LLC v. Schuler, No. 26-3196) with a related Tennessee appeal, uniting two cases that produced conflicting lower-court rulings on whether states can regulate sports event contracts offered on federally regulated exchanges.
items.source_label: Gambling Insider (June 19, 2026 weekly roundup)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market operators, event-contract platforms, CFTC registrants, sportsbooks

items.issuing_body: Cayuga Nation (plaintiff) — U.S. District Court, Northern District of New York
items.title: Cayuga Nation sues Caesars Sportsbook over mobile bets placed on tribal land — first tribal lawsuit against licensed sportsbook; novel IGRA 'where is the bet placed' geolocation theory
items.facts: On June 16, 2026, the Cayuga Nation of New York filed a federal lawsuit against American Wagering, Inc. (d/b/a Caesars Sportsbook), alleging that Caesars accepted mobile sports wagers from people physically located on the Cayuga reservation without tribal authorization, a gaming compact, or federal oversight. The complaint alleges violations of the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act (IGRA). Gaming attorney Daniel Wallach identified this as the first known case of a tribe suing a state-licensed sportsbook over online bets placed from Indian lands.
items.source_label: Casino.org (Philip Conneller, June 18, 2026; confirmed by fingerlakes1.com, SBC Americas, BettorsInsider, CasinoBeats, CDC Gaming, iGamingToday)
items.relevant_to: licensed mobile sportsbook operators, payment processors handling mobile betting, geolocation and compliance technology vendors, tribal gaming operators

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate
items.title: U.S. Senate passes 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644) with statutory Fed CBDC ban through 2030; House concurrence vote pending
items.facts: On June 18, 2026, the U.S. Senate invoked cloture (84-8) and passed the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644). The bill includes a provision banning the Federal Reserve from issuing or creating a central bank digital currency (CBDC) through December 31, 2030. The amended bill returns to the House for concurrence in the Senate amendment.
items.source_label: U.S. Senate Daily Press (June 18, 2026; corroborated by NACo and Latham Watkins analysis)
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, payment and fintech platforms, banks, digital-dollar infrastructure providers

items.issuing_body: U.S. District Court, W.D. Michigan (Judge Paul Maloney)
items.title: W.D. Michigan denies Robinhood preliminary injunction — sports event contracts are NOT swaps; CEA does not clearly preempt state gambling law
items.facts: On June 18, 2026, U.S. District Judge Paul Maloney denied Robinhood's motion for a preliminary injunction against Michigan state gambling enforcement. The court held: (1) sports event contracts are not 'swaps' under the Commodity Exchange Act; and (2) even if they were swaps, it is not clearly established that the CEA would preempt Michigan's state gambling law.
items.source_label: Gambling Insider (June 18, 2026; corroborated by Decrypt)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market operators, event-contract platforms, brokerages offering sports contracts, state gaming regulators

items.issuing_body: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
items.title: Sixth Circuit denies CFTC motion to participate as amicus at oral argument in KalshiEx v. Schuler (No. 26-3196)
items.facts: On June 16, 2026, the Sixth Circuit denied the CFTC's motion to appear as amicus curiae at oral argument in KalshiEx LLC v. Matthew T. Schuler et al. (No. 26-3196). The CFTC had submitted a written amicus brief on May 12, 2026, asserting exclusive CFTC jurisdiction over prediction markets.
items.source_label: SBC Americas (June 17, 2026); confirmed by Law360
items.relevant_to: prediction-market operators, event-contract platforms, CFTC-registered entities

items.issuing_body: Federal Reserve, OCC, FDIC, NCUA, and Treasury (FinCEN)
items.title: Five federal agencies propose a customer identification program rule for payment stablecoin issuers (GENIUS Act)
items.facts: On June 18, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board — jointly with the OCC, FDIC, NCUA, and Treasury/FinCEN — requested comment on a proposed rule requiring permitted payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs) to maintain an effective customer identification program (CIP). Comments are due 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.
items.source_label: Federal Reserve Board Press Release (June 18, 2026); joint with OCC, FDIC, NCUA, and Treasury/FinCEN.
items.relevant_to: payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs), crypto exchanges and custodians, banks and credit unions entering stablecoins, BSA/AML and compliance teams

items.issuing_body: State of Illinois (Gov. JB Pritzker)
items.title: Illinois enacts first-in-nation digital-asset transaction tax (SB 3019 / Digital Asset Tax Act)
items.facts: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed Senate Bill 3019, the Digital Asset Tax Act (DATA), as part of the state's $55.9 billion budget, making Illinois the first U.S. state to impose a transaction-based tax on digital-asset activity. The law imposes a 0.2% privilege tax on brokers who exchange, transfer, or store digital assets for customers in the state; takes effect January 1, 2027.
items.source_label: Crypto Briefing (reporting Illinois SB 3019 / Digital Asset Tax Act; signing also reported by Yahoo Finance, Bitcoin Magazine, The Defiant)
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, brokers, custodians and wallet providers with Illinois nexus; payment processors; tax/compliance teams

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate Banking Committee (Congress)
items.title: Congress folds a statutory Fed CBDC ban (through 2030) into the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644)
items.facts: On June 16, 2026, the leaders of the Senate Banking and House Financial Services Committees released updated bill text for H.R. 6644, folding in a statutory ban on a Federal Reserve central bank digital currency (CBDC) through December 31, 2030.
items.source_label: U.S. Senate Banking Committee Press Release (June 16, 2026)
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, payment and fintech platforms, banks, digital-dollar infrastructure providers

items.issuing_body: Tribal Amici (coalition of federally recognized tribes)
items.title: Tribal coalition files amicus briefs opposing CFTC/Kalshi preemption of tribal gaming laws
items.facts: A coalition of federally recognized tribes filed amicus briefs in two federal prediction-market cases, arguing that allowing Kalshi and the CFTC to override state gaming laws would also nullify tribal-state gaming compacts. The coalition filed in KalshiEx LLC v. Schuler (Sixth Circuit) and in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.
items.source_label: The Defiant (reporting the Tribal Amici amicus briefs; corroborated by Protos)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market / event-contract platforms, tribal gaming operators, sportsbooks, exchanges

items.issuing_body: CFTC
items.title: CFTC enters final consent order against Celsius Network and CEO Mashinsky — civil fraud, CEL token manipulation, and unregistered pool charges resolved; DOJ criminal case continues
items.facts: On June 18, 2026, the CFTC entered a final consent order against Celsius Network LLC and its former CEO Alex Mashinsky resolving civil enforcement claims. The consent order resolves: (1) fraudulent misrepresentation; (2) market manipulation of the CEL token; and (3) operating as an unregistered commodity pool operator. The DOJ's separate criminal case against Mashinsky continues.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9256-26
items.relevant_to: crypto lending platforms, token issuers, crypto exchanges, platform executives

items.issuing_body: CFTC and SEC
items.title: CFTC and SEC issue joint Request for Information on event contracts and prediction markets (Release 9258-26)
items.facts: On June 18, 2026, the CFTC and SEC jointly issued Release 9258-26, a Request for Information on event-based contracts and the application of existing regulatory frameworks to prediction markets. This is the first joint inter-agency RFI on the jurisdictional classification of event contracts and prediction markets.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9258-26
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, event-contract operators, crypto exchanges, derivatives platforms

items.issuing_body: CFTC and SEC
items.title: CFTC and SEC issue joint Request for Information on derivatives data reporting modernization (Release 9257-26)
items.facts: On June 18, 2026, the CFTC and SEC jointly issued Release 9257-26, a Request for Information on derivatives data reporting and regulatory technology modernization covering swap data repository (SDR) reporting, real-time public reporting of swap transaction data, and new data-field standards.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9257-26
items.relevant_to: derivatives market participants, swap data repositories, crypto derivatives platforms, CFTC registrants

items.issuing_body: CME Group — U.S. District Court
items.title: CME Group sues CFTC over approval of perpetual bitcoin futures (BTCPERP) on Kalshi — argues perps are swaps not futures; challenges 24-hour self-certification as APA violation
items.facts: CME Group filed suit against the CFTC challenging the agency's June 2026 approval of Bitcoin perpetual futures contracts (BTCPERP) on KalshiEx via the CFTC's Regulation 40.2 self-certification process. CME argues: (1) perpetual futures contracts are 'swaps' under the CEA rather than futures; and (2) using the 24-hour self-certification process violated the APA's notice-and-comment requirements.
items.source_label: Markets Media (reporting the CME Group v. CFTC lawsuit)
items.relevant_to: crypto derivatives platforms, perpetual futures operators, Kalshi, Coinbase, CFTC registrants

items.issuing_body: U.S. District Court, W.D. Michigan
items.title: W.D. Michigan denies Polymarket PI — court rules sports event contracts are NOT 'swaps' under the CEA; CEA may not preempt state gambling law even if they were
items.facts: On June 17, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Michigan denied Polymarket's motion for a preliminary injunction against enforcement of Michigan state gambling law. The court held: (1) sports event contracts are not 'swaps' under the CEA; and (2) even if they were swaps, it is not clearly established that the CEA would preempt Michigan's state gambling law.
items.source_label: SBC Americas (reporting the W.D. Michigan PI denial)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, event-contract operators, state gaming regulators, sportsbooks

items.issuing_body: NYDFS
items.title: NYDFS proposes stablecoin regulation aligning New York's framework with the federal GENIUS Act
items.facts: On June 9, 2026, the New York State Department of Financial Services, under Acting Superintendent Kaitlin Asrow, proposed a regulation to build on New York's existing stablecoin framework and align it with the federal GENIUS Act. The proposed regulation is subject to a 10-day preproposal comment period beginning June 9, 2026, followed by a 60-day comment period upon publication in the State Register.
items.source_label: NYDFS Press Release (June 9, 2026)
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, virtual-currency (BitLicense) licensees, custodians, payment-stablecoin platforms

items.issuing_body: CFTC
items.title: CFTC issues Request for Information on fintech innovation, AI, and digital asset technologies (Release 9254-26)
items.facts: On June 16, 2026, the CFTC issued Release 9254-26, a Request for Information on fintech innovation, artificial intelligence, and digital asset technologies. The RFI covers DeFi protocols, AI/ML applications in trading, real-world asset (RWA) tokenization, payment stablecoins as margin/collateral, and cybersecurity.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9254-26
items.relevant_to: DeFi protocols, crypto exchanges, stablecoin issuers, AI trading firms, RWA tokenization platforms

items.issuing_body: Pennsylvania Supreme Court
items.title: Pennsylvania Supreme Court rules skill games are slot machines; 120-day enforcement stay issued
items.facts: On June 15, 2026, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court issued its majority opinion in J-97-2025 (Pace-O-Matic v. Pennsylvania), ruling that skill game machines 'are subject to both the Gaming Act and the Crimes Code,' overturning a Commonwealth Court ruling. The Court issued a 120-day enforcement stay. An estimated 70,000+ skill game machines operate in bars, VFWs, restaurants, and fraternal clubs statewide.
items.source_label: Pennsylvania Supreme Court Opinion J-97-2025 (majority opinion)
items.relevant_to: skill game operators, gaming venues (bars, VFWs, fraternal clubs), payment processors, PA legislators

items.issuing_body: State of Wisconsin (Attorney General) — U.S. District Court, W.D. Wis.
items.title: Wisconsin moves to block sports event-contract trading on Coinbase, Kalshi, and Robinhood
items.facts: On 2026-06-09, the State of Wisconsin filed a motion for a preliminary injunction seeking to block KalshiEx, Coinbase, and Robinhood from offering sports event-contract trading to people in the state until the court rules on the merits of its underlying lawsuit.
items.source_label: DeFi Rate (reporting the Wisconsin preliminary-injunction motion)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, crypto exchanges, brokerages

items.issuing_body: Gary Gensler (amicus) — U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
items.title: Gensler files Sixth Circuit amicus arguing sports prediction markets are not 'swaps'
items.facts: On 2026-06-11, former CFTC and SEC chair Gary Gensler filed an amicus brief with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit in KalshiEx LLC v. Schuler, arguing that sports-event prediction-market contracts fall outside the statutory definition of a 'swap' under Dodd-Frank and are therefore not within the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction.
items.source_label: The Defiant (reporting the Gensler Sixth Circuit amicus brief)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, derivatives exchanges, crypto exchanges

items.issuing_body: Delaware General Assembly (HB 441) / New Jersey Legislature (S-2141)
items.title: Delaware (HB 441) and New Jersey (S-2141) advance statewide crypto-ATM bans
items.facts: Delaware and New Jersey have each advanced legislation to ban cryptocurrency ATMs statewide, citing fraud losses. Delaware's House Bill 441 passed the House; it would require existing kiosks to go dark upon enactment and be physically removed within 90 days. New Jersey's Senate Bill S-2141 cleared the Senate Commerce Committee unanimously.
items.source_label: The Defiant (reporting the Delaware and New Jersey crypto-ATM ban bills)
items.relevant_to: crypto-ATM/kiosk operators, payment processors, compliance vendors

items.issuing_body: Financial Technology Association v. Tennessee — Davidson County Chancery Court
items.title: Fintech trade group sues Tennessee to block remittance tax (HB2502)
items.facts: The Financial Technology Association filed suit in Davidson County (Tennessee) Chancery Court seeking an injunction to block HB2502, a law signed by Gov. Bill Lee in May 2026 that adds a $10 fee on monetary wire transfers to another country plus a 2% tax on transfers over $500 (effective Jan. 1, 2027). The FTA argues the law is unconstitutional under the dormant Commerce Clause.
items.source_label: The Center Square (reporting the FTA v. Tennessee filing)
items.relevant_to: money transmitters, remittance providers, payment processors, fintechs

items.issuing_body: CFTC
items.title: CFTC sues New Mexico over prediction-market preemption (8th state)
items.facts: On 2026-06-12 the CFTC filed suit in federal court against the State of New Mexico, seeking a declaratory judgment that federal law grants it exclusive authority over event contracts and a permanent injunction barring the state from enforcing preempted gaming laws against CFTC registrants. New Mexico joins AZ, CT, IL, NY, MN, RI, and WI.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9251-26
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, sportsbooks, exchanges, CFTC registrants

items.issuing_body: Nevada Gaming Control Board
items.title: Nevada gaming regulator seeks to hold Kalshi in contempt over prediction-market geofencing
items.facts: On 2026-06-12 the Nevada Gaming Control Board petitioned the First Judicial District Court in Carson City to find KalshiEx LLC in contempt for allegedly not complying with a May 18 order requiring it to geofence its website so it cannot offer sports-, election-, or entertainment-related event contracts to anyone located in Nevada.
items.source_label: Las Vegas Review-Journal (reporting the Nevada GCB court filing)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, geolocation/compliance vendors, sportsbooks

items.issuing_body: Coalition for Fair Markets (NADEX, Kalshi, Polymarket/QCX)
items.title: Prediction-market coalition sues Kentucky over 14.25% tax on event-contract trading
items.facts: On 2026-06-12, the Coalition for Fair Markets — comprising Crypto.com's North American Derivatives Exchange (NADEX), Kalshi, and Polymarket's U.S. exchange QCX — filed suit in Franklin Circuit Court to block Kentucky from implementing a 14.25% tax on prediction-market transaction fees set to take effect Jan. 1, 2027.
items.source_label: SBC Americas (reporting the Coalition for Fair Markets filing; first reported by the Associated Press)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, licensed gaming operators, payment processors
